In [[algebra]], a [[filtered ring]] ''A'' is said to be '''almost commutative''' if the associated [[graded ring]] <math>\operatorname{gr}A = \oplus A_i/{A_{i-1}}</math> is [[commutative ring|commutative]].

Basic examples of almost commutative rings involve [[differential operator]]s. For example, the enveloping algebra of a complex [[Lie algebra]] is almost commutative by the [[PBW theorem]]. Similarly, a [[Weyl algebra]] is almost commutative.
